_note: Pre-registered deployment gates, in the spirit of DuckBench's GATES.md: written before the
measurements so the decision later is a lookup rather than an argument.
Condition names and their levels come from microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py (the envelope the
policy is trained in) and duckbench/PLANT.md (the torque ceiling and solver), not from taste.
A policy that fails an envelope condition has a real gap; failing a beyond-envelope stress
condition is information, not necessarily a blocker.
tracking_min is measured speed divided by commanded speed, median over envs.
falls_max is total falls across all envs in the run, resets included.
_revision: The numbers below are deliberately left exactly as first registered. Re-editing a gate after
seeing the measurement would turn a decision into a rationalisation, which is the failure
mode GATES.md exists to prevent. Read the note instead, and read the number again.
CORRECTION (see README, 'delay is how much'): the latency_* gate levels were chosen while
the actuator lag was misread as control periods (3-6 periods = 60-120 ms). mjlab quantises
delay_min_lag / delay_max_lag to PHYSICS timesteps, so upstream's 3-6 is 6-12 ms at 500 Hz.
Consequently latency_40ms and above are BEYOND the trained envelope, not inside it: they are
stress conditions, and the low numbers there are a finding about our policy, not a statement
that a working robot needs to hit them. latency_20ms remains the only latency gate that a
deployable policy must pass, since a Pi under load can plausibly add a whole period.
obs_lag_official was added to robustness.py after these gates were registered, so it has no
gate above. Recording it now, before the next full run measures it: obs_lag_official and
obs_delay_20ms are held to the same level (tracking_min 0.55, falls_max 2), because the
per-term lag IS the model of the real sensor path -- it is the one latency condition that
is in envelope by construction, not a stress test.
STRUCTURAL CAVEAT: `nominal` means no delay at all. On hardware there is always at least the
firmware's one-period joint-velocity lag, so a policy trained for the real loop is OUT OF
DISTRIBUTION at `nominal` and can fail it while passing obs_lag_official. Measured exactly
that: robust61_a scores 0.438 at nominal and 0.801 at obs_lag_official. Do not decide
deployability by counting PASSes; read the obs_lag_official row for the loop condition and
the plant rows for the physics, separately.
MEASUREMENT BUG, 2026-10-23: `rollout()` built its action-delay line as
deque(zeros * act_delay, maxlen=act_delay). Appending into a full deque evicts the oldest
entry first, so popleft returned the action that had just been appended and every latency_*
condition ran one rung short: latency_20ms was bit-for-bit the nominal run (identical
tracking, tilt and heading error on every policy -- that identity was the tell), and
latency_N ms actually measured (N-20) ms. The fix is maxlen=act_delay+1. Consequence for
these gates: no latency number recorded before this date is at the level its name says.
Re-measured after the fix, robust61_a at 0.3 m/s over 8 s x 8 envs x 3 seeds:
0 ms 0.438, 20 ms 0.396, 40 ms 0.388, 60 ms 0.245 with 29 falls and 47 deg tilt,
80 ms 0.503 with 56 falls (a tracking ratio measured on a robot lying on its side is not a
tracking ratio; the falls column has to be read first). So latency_20ms now has a real
number and it still passes 0.65's *neighbour*: it is below it, 0.396 < 0.65, i.e. this gate
now FAILS. It was never passing; it was never measured.
AGGREGATION, 2026-10-23: with --seeds > 1 the falls column is the WORST seed (a failure that
happens once is a failure) and tracking is the mean across seeds, with the spread printed.
One seed over 8 envs x 8 s is 64 s of robot time and cannot separate a reliable policy from
a lucky one; the levels above were registered on single-seed runs and are therefore looser
than they look.
2026-10-23 (later) -- plant-DR: four runs, zero positive results, and none of them are about
plant DR. `robust61_dr` / `dr5` / `drm` trained at track 0.87 / 0.81 / 0.79 and evaluate at
tracking ratio 0.438 / 0.297 / 0.002. The last one is a frozen standing pose (tilt 1.3 deg,
zero falls). The training `track` number spans 0.79-0.87 across policies whose true tracking
differs by 200x, so it could never have reported that collapse -- exp(-0.09/0.25) = 0.698 is
what standing still scores. `train_ppo.rollout` now logs `v` (achieved/commanded velocity,
same definition as the eval's tracking_ratio) in the progress line for exactly this reason.
Correction to the `lpf_leg45` entry: those numbers do NOT show that an action low-pass is
useless. Upstream AGENTS.md states policies are trained unfiltered and that adding an EMA on
one side only (either direction) breaks transfer. We applied the filter at eval time to a
policy trained without it, so the 0.383 -> 0.278 measures the mismatch we introduced. Test a
filter by training with it, not by bolting it on afterwards.
Also from AGENTS.md, verified rather than assumed: obs normalisation IS on here, and
`export_mcu.py` does bake md_mean / md_inv_std into the C header, so the MCU artefact is not
missing it; `_draw_plant` writes absolute base*scale values, so plant DR does not accumulate
across resets. Both are the upstream footguns we happened to avoid -- checked, not lucky.
2026-10-23 (third pass) -- THE TRACKING KERNEL WAS WRONG IN TWO DIRECTIONS, and one of
them silently zeroed the turn reward. `train_ppo.SIGMA` was a single 0.25 for both axes.
Upstream (`microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:342-345`) sets track weight 2.0 with
`std=sqrt(0.1)` and turn weight 2.0 with `std=sqrt(0.5)`, and mjlab's reward is
`exp(-error / std**2)` -- verified in mjlab/tasks/velocity/mdp/rewards.py, not inferred
from the docs. So the upstream denominators are 0.10 (linear) and 0.50 (angular).
Linear 0.25 vs 0.10: a motionless robot against 0.3 m/s scored exp(-0.09/0.25) = 0.698
here against 0.407 upstream. Angular 0.25 vs 0.50: yaw error routinely reaches 0.5-1.0
rad/s, where a 0.25 kernel is already at exp(-4) = 0.018. The turn term was SATURATED, so
it could not teach anything -- which is the real explanation for the `--track-weight 3`
run where turn fell 0.24 -> 0.08 and yaw went +0.78 -> -0.03. That was not 'turning got
penalised', it was 'the turning term went flat and stopped pulling'.
Now SIGMA_LIN=0.10 / SIGMA_ANG=0.50, with --sigma-lin / --sigma-ang to override and
--sigma kept only to reproduce pre-split runs (it forces both to one value, i.e. the old
bug). EVERY weight trained before this note -- robust61_a, _n, _s, _dr, _dr5, _drm, _drmb
-- used 0.25/0.25, so none of them was ever rewarded for turning correctly. Compare them
by the eval's tracking_ratio (kernel-independent) and treat any 'it will not turn' finding
as a reward artefact first.
Two more upstream reward terms we simply do not have, both now sourced: `air_time` 3.0
(foot air time must land in 0.125-0.3 s, which is what forces alternating steps instead
of dragging) and `foot_slip` -0.1 on the stance foot, deliberately weak because a strong
slip penalty prevents in-place turning. Missing air_time is the most likely single reason
a policy can score well while never lifting a foot.
2026-10-23 (fourth pass) -- FOURTH SILENT BUG, and this one was in the reward, not the
measurement. `Duck.__init__` did `self.foot = self.site[:, self.feet]`. `self.feet` is a
LIST, so that is fancy indexing and COPIES; `site_xpos` is only written by mj_forward /
mj_step, and __init__ runs before either, so the copy froze at all zeros. Every consumer
of foot height read 0.0 forever:
- `gait` (weight 1.0) -- with height identically 0, `swing = exp(-low^2/WIDTH^2)` and
`stance = exp(0) = 1` depend only on the phase clock and `moving()`. The term became a
pure function of time: no gradient, and it still logged 0.83, which looks like a healthy
gait reward. A weight-1.0 term has been contributing a constant offset to every run.
- `BallBalance`'s `feet_mid` -- same zero buffer, so the ball task's foot midpoint was
pinned to the origin.
- `air_time` (added this pass) -- would have been identically zero, i.e. a dead new term
that looked like 'the policy never lifts its feet'.
Measured before the fix: foot-site z p0..p100 all exactly 0.00 mm over 300 steps, while
`site_xpos` at those same ids read 0.011-0.013 m. After: p50 = 0.83 mm, p90 = 9.29 mm,
p99 = 28.98 mm, 12.5% of foot-samples above the 8 mm lift threshold.
`self.rot` three lines above is `self.xmat[:, self.trunk]` -- basic indexing with an INT,
which stays a live view. Identical-looking line, opposite semantics; that is exactly why
nobody looked at it. `foot` is now a property that re-reads `site_xpos` each access.
`tools/selfcheck.py` grew `check_foot` (3 assertions: not all-zero, agrees with site_xpos,
changes across a step) plus `break_foot_cache`, which reinstates the all-zero property and
requires all 3 to go red. Now 23/23 with the negative control green.
Consequence for the record: every weight up to and including `robust61_drmb` was trained
with `gait` as a constant. Do not compare reward magnitudes across this boundary -- the
reward scale itself changed, even though the gait the policies produced was real (the legs
were driven by `track` and `pose`, not by `gait`).
2026-10-23 (fifth pass) -- `gait` is OUR invention, upstream has no gait phase clock.
Listed every upstream reward term in `microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py`: pose 1.0, upright 2.0
(std=sqrt(0.05)), body_ang_vel -0.05, angular_momentum -0.02, foot_slip -0.1,
self_collisions -1.0, air_time 3.0 (window 0.125-0.300 s), track_linear 2.0 (std=sqrt(0.1)),
track_angular 2.0 (std=sqrt(0.5)), action_rate_l2 -0.1, foot_clearance (target 0.02),
foot_swing_height (target 0.02). There is no reference-phase term anywhere. Gait shape
emerges from air_time + foot_clearance + tracking; it is never told a frequency.
Ours (`train_ppo.py:265-268`) drives `gait` from `sin(2*pi*clock)` at GAIT_HZ=1.5 with
weight 1.0, i.e. it prescribes a 667 ms cycle. That is a constraint upstream does not
impose, and it is ~22% of total reward (0.80 of 3.64 at iter 57 of robust61_k1). Keep it
for now as a bootstrap, but if a policy ever stalls at a gait that matches the clock and
still scores well while failing on hardware, this term is the first suspect. The upstream
replacement is two terms: foot_clearance and foot_swing_height, both target 0.02 m.
Checked and cleared rather than assumed: GAIT_HZ=1.5 does NOT conflict with the 0.125-0.300 s
air_time window. A foot counts as airborne above 0.008 m, i.e. sin(phase) > 0.4, which spans
74% of the 333 ms stance->swing half-cycle = 246 ms -- inside the window. So a policy that
actually tracks the sine gets paid. The measured air_time of 0.02 (robust61_a: p90 foot
height 9.29 mm, only 12.5% of samples above 8 mm) means the policy lifts far too little,
not that the window is misconfigured. Do not widen the window to make the number look better.
BAM, two things verified by running it rather than reading about it:
- `bam.mujoco.MujocoController.update()` is single-instance (reads qpos/qvel/qfrc_bias,
writes ctrl for one mjModel+mjData). 2048 envs means 2048 Python objects and 2048
per-step method calls, ~5 s per iteration against a 7 s iteration -- it would cost more
throughput than mjbatch gains. The formulas must be vectorised, not called per env.
- BAM parameters cannot be back-solved from datasheets. Applying the xl330 `m6` params
(kt=0.366, R=2.81) to its own 5 V stall spec gives 0.651 N.m against a 0.40 N.m
datasheet value -- 1.6x high. Same method on HD-1910 (kt=1.47/2.0, R=8.4/2.0) inherits
that error. Identification needs a bench, which is also why upstream says actuator
fidelity is most of the sim2real gap.
- `better-actuator-models` is NOT on the Tsinghua mirror; `pip install -i https://pypi.org/simple`
is required. Installed 1.0.1 here, deps clean (only colorama added).
2026-10-23 (sixth pass) -- THE REWARD WAS WRONG IN THREE MORE PLACES, and all three made
a sloppy stance cheaper than a correct one. Found by rendering the upstream `pose` and
`upright` implementations from `microduck/tasks/mdp.py` instead of reading the weight table.
1. `pose` used `exp(-sum((q - q_stand)**2))`. Upstream is
`exp(-mean((q - q_stand)**2 / std**2))` with a PER-JOINT std (`mdp.py:5447-5449`,
stds from `microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:199-217`). Two differences at once: mean not
sum, and divided by a tolerance as small as 0.05 rad (hip_roll). Measured on
`robust61_a`: ours reported ~0.9, upstream's formula reports 0.64 for the same pose.
So the pose term was barely constraining anything, and 'pose 0.9' in old logs meant
nothing.
2. `upright` was `exp(-2*(up_x^2+up_y^2))`. Upstream is `exp(-err/std**2)` with
`std = sqrt(0.05)`, i.e. `exp(-40*(qx^2+qy^2))` -- the `/0.05` was simply missing.
A 10 deg tilt scored 0.98 here versus 0.30 upstream. The upright term was decoration.
3. Every positive weight was small: track 1.0 vs upstream 2.0, turn 0.5 vs 2.0,
pose 0.5 vs 1.0, upright 1.0 vs 2.0. Positives summed to 4.5 against -1.605 of
penalties (ratio 2.8); upstream is 10.0 against -1.27 (ratio 7.9). Combined with (1)
and (2), the reward actively preferred the conservative motionless solution: the
tracking term paid 0.407 for standing still, and every regulariser paid full marks for
not moving.
`--upstream-rewards` now applies the whole set in one flag: weights track 2.0 / turn 2.0 /
pose 1.0 / upright 2.0 / air_time 3.0 / rate -0.1, the corrected pose and upright formulas,
and ZERO for every term upstream does not have (gait, height, slab, torque, limits).
`gait` is the costly one to drop -- it was a 667 ms reference clock at weight 1.0, so gait
shape now has to come from air_time alone, which is sparse (0/1/2 per step).
Note for future comparisons: `turn` is now 2.0 with SIGMA_ANG 0.50, i.e. 4x the weight and
twice the kernel width of the pre-split setting. A yaw error of 1.0 rad/s earns 0.135*2.0
= 0.27 instead of the original 0.018*0.5 = 0.009. The turning signal is now ~30x stronger,
which is the first configuration where 'the policy will not turn' can be read as anything
other than a reward artefact.
Also measured while checking this: `np.where(speed < 0.01, STD_14, STD_14B)` raises
`operands could not be broadcast (4096,) (14,) (14,)` -- the condition needs a `[:, None]`,
same class of mistake as the foot-cache bug. Caught by the smoke run, not by review.
2026-10-23 (seventh pass) -- the observation contract was audited and is correct. Worth
recording because during the audit it briefly looked broken: there are TWO environment
classes. `train_ppo.Duck` is 56-D and includes two clock columns (sin/cos of the gait
phase) plus pre-scaled features (2*vel, 0.25*gyro, 0.05*qvel). `train_official.Duck`
subclasses it and replaces `obs()` with the 61-D deployable vector:
gyro(3) | gravity(3) | joint_pos - stand(14) | joint_vel(14) | action(14) | command(13)
no clock, no pre-scaling, joint_pos relative to `stand`, command = 3 twist + 4 head zeros
+ 6 body zeros. That is byte-for-byte the layout upstream describes, and the assert at
`train_official.py:56` (`3 + 3 + 14*3 + 3 + 4 + 6 == 61`) is what keeps it honest.
`train_robust` registers itself into `T.TASKS['velocity']`, so every robust run trains the
61-D class -- verified by reading the registry, not assumed.
So the observation side has no defect. The defects found today are all on the reward side
(kernel, pose formula, upright formula, weights) plus the foot-site cache. Stating the
negative result explicitly matters: 'we checked X and X is fine' is the only thing that
stops the same audit being redone from scratch next month.
2026-10-23 (eighth pass) -- MY OWN FIX WAS 4x TOO STRICT, and the self-check I wrote to
guard it could not catch that. This is the most instructive failure of the day.
Correcting `upright` from `exp(-2*up_err)` to upstream's `exp(-err/std**2)` with
`std**2 = 0.05`, I wrote `exp(-2*up_err/0.05)` -- i.e. divided by 0.05 but kept the 2.
Upstream's `err` is `tilt_sq = 2*(qx**2+qy**2) = 1 - cos(tilt)`; ours is
`up_err = up_x**2 + up_y**2 = sin^2(tilt)`. Measured at 10 deg: 0.015192 vs 0.030154 --
exactly 2:1. So `tilt_sq = 0.5*up_err` and the correct term is `exp(-0.5*up_err/0.05)`.
The version I shipped was `exp(-4*tilt_sq/0.05)`, 4x upstream's, scoring 0.299 at 10 deg
where upstream scores 0.738.
Effect, measured: `robust61_u1` (the 4x version) tracked at `v`/cmd = 8% and `air_time`
fell to 0.02 -- MORE conservative than `robust61_k1` was, despite every other change
pointing the right way. A policy punished that hard for a 10 deg lean cannot afford to
walk, because walking is a controlled fall. `robust61_u2` (corrected, nothing else
changed) starts at reward 5.01 vs 4.74, track 0.70 vs 0.63, air_time 0.04 vs 0.01.
The self-check is the real lesson. I wrote:
check('upright at 10 deg scores under 0.35', tight_up < 0.35, ...)
which asserts the term got STRICTER. It did -- 4x too strict and still passed. An
assertion of the form 'moved in the right direction' cannot detect overshoot. It is now:
check('upright matches upstream 1-cos(tilt) at 10 deg within 2%', ...)
check('upright is stricter than the legacy exp(-2*up_err)', ...)
the first of which is an equivalence test against the reference formula and would have
failed immediately at 0.299 vs 0.738.
Generalise: when porting a formula from a reference implementation, the check must compare
VALUES against that reference at a few operating points, not compare against the buggy
version we are replacing. Direction-of-change is not correctness.
Also re-verified in the same pass, since two derivations disagreed: `up = -rot[:, 2]` on the
(N,3,3) array IS the gravity direction in the body frame. Checked by tilting one env 10 deg
and comparing against `R.T @ [0,0,-1]`: identical to 1e-6. The confusion came from testing
`rot[0][:, 2]` (column of a 2-D array) instead of `rot[:, 2]` (row of a 3-D array) -- the
same basic-vs-advanced indexing trap as the foot-cache bug, this time in my own probe.
2026-10-23 (ninth pass) -- THE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG, and my own probe was the reason. The
policy does not fail to walk; it fails to walk STRAIGHT.
`train_ppo.rollout` reported achieved speed as `qvel[:, :2] . cmd_xy`. `qvel[:2]` is
WORLD-frame (free joint) while `cmd` is BODY-frame, so that dot is scaled by
cos(heading error) and reads exactly 0 at 90 deg of heading. Measured on `robust61_a`:
old 0.0312 m/s (15.9% of command) vs body-frame 0.0500 m/s (25.5%) -- under-reported 1.6x.
Every 'v collapsed / no trend' judgement made earlier today used that number, so treat
those readings as a floor, not a measurement. Fixed by rotating with `einsum('nji,nj->ni',
rot, qvel[:, :3])` first, matching what the `track` term already did.
With the corrected number the error decomposes cleanly. `robust61_a`, noise off, 200 steps:
commanded 0.197 m/s, achieved 0.050 m/s forward, `track` term 0.712. A track of 0.712 with
SIGMA_LIN 0.10 implies an xy error of sqrt(0.10*|ln 0.712|) = 0.184 m/s. Forward error is
only 0.146, so ~0.11 m/s of the error is LATERAL -- larger than the forward speed itself.
That matches the eval exactly: `lateral_m_median` 0.436 m over 8 s = 0.055 m/s of drift and
`heading_error_deg_median` 22.4 deg. Two independent measurements, same conclusion.
So the priority order from earlier today was wrong. Foot lifting (air_time/clearance) and
forward speed are secondary; heading and lateral control dominate the loss. `turn` going
from weight 0.5 / kernel 0.25 to 2.0 / 0.50 is the change that addresses the actual
problem -- a yaw error of 1.0 rad/s now earns 0.27 instead of 0.009.
This also explains why every fine-tune lowered the `track` term (a 0.87 -> k1 0.74 ->
u2/u3 0.66): the added regularisers (`upright` 2.0, `pose` 1.0, `clearance` -2.0) buy
stability by suppressing exactly the lateral/yaw motion that would fix the error, if the
yaw channel is not strong enough to steer it. Watch `turn` and the eval's
`heading_error_deg_median`, NOT `track`.
Still-open question worth stating: `robust61_a` trains at `track` 0.87 but evaluates at
tracking_ratio 0.438 with 22 deg of heading error. A high `track` term alongside visible
drift means the term is being satisfied in the mean while the drift is unchecked -- the
kernel sees xy error but not the heading state, so a policy can oscillate/curve and still
score. Do not treat `track` as a heading metric.

THE DATA WAS ONLINE THE WHOLE TIME. Every number I spent three rounds inferring is in two public packages: `pollen-robotics/microduck_rl` @ `develop` (task-level overrides, `microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:275-356`) and PyPI `mjlab==1.3.0` (the kernels, `src/mjlab/tasks/velocity/mdp/rewards.py`). What I was doing instead was re-deriving them from prose. Transcribed into `.upstream/UPSTREAM_REWARD_SPEC.md` with file:line citations. Note the default branch is `develop` -- `master` and `main` both 404 on the raw host.

`upright`: I was wrong in BOTH directions and each time my selfcheck agreed with me. I first read upstream as `exp(-tilt_sq/std^2)` with `tilt_sq = 2(qx^2+qy^2) = 1-cos(tilt)`, decided our `sin^2(tilt)` was 2x larger, and multiplied by 0.5 to 'convert'. The source uses neither quaternions nor 1-cos: `gravity_vec_w` is literally `[0,0,-1.0]` (`entity/entity.py:787`), so `sum(square(projected_gravity_b[:, :2]))` IS `sin^2(tilt)`, divided by `std^2` and nothing else. My 0.5 made the term 2x too permissive -- 0.740 at 10 deg against upstream's 0.547 -- i.e. the opposite of the direction I had reasoned to, and `robust61_u1..u3` all ran on it. The selfcheck passed because it asserted `ours == exp(-(1-cos)/0.05)`, comparing the port against MY DESCRIPTION of upstream instead of upstream. Rule adopted: an assertion about a ported formula must reproduce the reference implementation's own numbers.

The two curricula are the reason a 600-iteration run was never 'the upstream recipe', and I did not know they existed. `action_rate_l2` ramps -0.1 -> -1.0 over stages 0/500/750/1000/1250/1500, and `rel_standing_envs` ramps 0.02 -> 0.25 over 0/500/750/1000/1500/2000 (`microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:778-805`, `step` units converted with NUM_STEPS_PER_ENV=24). At iter 600 the smoothing weight is -0.2 and only 5% of envs stand. We froze `rate` at -0.1 for every run and evaluated the result as if it were finished. Implemented as `--curriculum`.

'Walks but drifts' is not a bug in our port -- it is the recipe's own blind spot, and there is a published mechanism for it that upstream deliberately leaves OFF. mjlab has a heading-control mode (`mdp/velocity_command.py:117-122`): for `is_heading_env` fraction, `command[:, 2]` is replaced by `heading_control_stiffness * wrap_to_pi(target - heading_w)`, so `track_angular_velocity` silently becomes a heading-error-cancelling reward. No reward change, no extra observation -- the command's third slot carries the information. Upstream sets `rel_heading_envs = 0.0` for the walk task. Corroborated by the HD1910 replica report that official weights still yaw-drift on correctly adapted hardware.

Filled the three missing terms and restored one I had wrongly zeroed: `foot_slip` (-0.1, `sum(||v_foot_xy||^2 * in_contact)`), `foot_swing_height` (-0.25, charged only on the landing edge as `sum((peak/target - 1)^2 * first_contact)`, target 0.02), and `dof_pos_limits` back to -1.0 -- the previous block zeroed `limits` alongside `gait/height/slab/torque`, but only those last four are absent upstream. Also added upstream's missing pieces in existing terms: the vertical `v_bz^2` inside `track`, and the roll/pitch rate `omega_x^2+omega_y^2` inside `turn`. The latter is large: `turn` read 0.55 on `robust61_a`, 0.17 once roll/pitch are priced.

Command sampling was also off upstream: ours was lin_x +-0.5 / yaw +-1.2 with per-axis sparsity (0.9/0.25/0.5), upstream is +-0.4 / +-0.3 / +-1.0 continuous plus a 15% turn-in-place quota, justified in their own comment as 'independent uniform sampling makes spin-on-the-spot ~2% of data -> untrained'. Implemented as `--upstream-commands`. The realised spin fraction is `turn_in_place * (1 - rel_standing)` because standing is drawn last and overwrites; that cost one red selfcheck before I wrote the overlap into the assertion.

Launched `robust61_u4`: 2000 iters, warm-started from `robust61_a`, full upstream recipe (`--upstream-rewards --curriculum --upstream-commands`). 2000 is the first iteration count at which both curricula have reached their final stage, which is the minimum bar for calling any result 'the upstream recipe'. selfcheck is 44/44.

SECOND AUDIT, and the reward list was not the whole story. Having claimed the reward table was now source-exact, I went back and checked every OTHER quantity that shapes behaviour: the observation contract, control timing, action scale, termination, observation noise, and the DR ranges. Four more mismatches. Every one of them would have survived a 2-hour run and then been blamed on the reward.

Termination was 24 deg tighter than upstream. Upstream is `bad_orientation(limit_angle=radians(70))` (`mjlab velocity_env_cfg.py:379-382`); ours was `up_z > -0.7`, i.e. cos(tilt) < 0.7 -> 45.57 deg. This is not a mild difference: the upright reward's own comment budgets for 'transient lean (push recovery, accel) stays affordable'. A 45 deg leash deletes that regime, so the policy can only learn never to lean, never to recover. Fixed to 70 deg via `FELL_COS`.

Observation noise had the wrong distribution AND a 9x wrong scale on one channel. Upstream is `Unoise(n_min, n_max)` -- uniform -- with half-widths gyro 0.03 / gravity 0.01 / joint_pos 0.001 / joint_vel 0.25. Ours was Gaussian sigmas 0.02 / 0.01 / 0.005 / 0.3. A uniform +-0.001 has sigma 0.00058, so our joint_pos noise was 8.7x upstream, injected on the channel the policy needs to hold hip_roll inside a 0.05 rad tolerance. Fixed to uniform half-widths; the selfcheck now differencing a noise=0 env against a noise=1 env of the same seed, which also makes the DISTRIBUTION testable (a Gaussian scaled to the same width exceeds that width somewhere in 2000 samples; a uniform cannot).

The head was in the wrong term with the wrong weight. Upstream keeps head/neck OUT of `pose` by regex, with a stated reason ('it would pull them to HOME while head_pose_tracking pulls them to the command, and the policy converges to ignore the command'), and gives the head its own `head_pose_tracking` at weight 2.0 / std 0.5. We averaged 14 joints including 4 head joints at an invented std 0.3 under weight 1.0. Because `pose` uses MEAN, that also weakened every leg tolerance by 10/14. Split: `pose` = 10 legs, `head` = 4 head joints at 2.0/0.5, plus `head_pose_bias` (L1 on a 1 s EMA, returns a NEGATIVE value, curriculum 0->1->2->3 at iter 0/600/1000/1500) which we did not have at all.

Actuator delay: upstream `delay_min_lag=3, delay_max_lag=6` in PHYSICS steps at 5 ms = 15-30 ms. Ours was `--act-delay 0,2` control periods = 0-40 ms, which includes ZERO delay -- a condition upstream never trains on. Changed to `1,2` (20-40 ms), the closest integer range to 0.75-1.5 control periods.

Two things were already right and I want them recorded so the next audit does not re-litigate them: the 61-D observation layout (`gyro, projected_gravity, joint_pos, joint_vel, actions, twist+head_pose+body_pose`, no base_lin_vel, no clock, no pre-scaling) matches upstream term for term and is pinned by an assert; and control rate (20 ms), episode (20 s), action scale (1.0) and rollout length (24) all match.

Explicitly NOT aligned, listed rather than approximated: `angular_momentum` (-0.02) needs a whole-body momentum sensor; `self_collisions` (-1.0) needs per-geom contact-force history; mass/inertia +-5%, CoM +-3mm, joint friction (0.9,1.1), armature (0.9,1.1), foot friction (0.7,1.3) and IMU mounting +-6 deg are all `plant_dr` work that this run leaves off. The spec file carries this table so the gaps cannot quietly become assumptions.

Restarted twice before settling: `u4` (2000 iters) was killed at ~150 iters when the termination and head-term gaps surfaced, `u5` at ~100 iters when the noise gap did. Correct call both times -- a run whose config is wrong is not cheap at 100 minutes, and the failure mode is a plausible-looking result blamed on the wrong term. `robust61_u6` is the first run with all of the above applied. selfcheck is 71/71.

CLOSING THE HEADING LOOP NEEDS NO RETRAINING. Zero-shot on `robust61_a` -- a policy trained with `rel_heading_envs = 0`, so it has never seen this control law -- the measured 8 s walk goes from 27.8 deg path error / 0.448 m lateral, to 4.3 deg / 0.089 m, and mean yaw rate from -0.116 to -0.016 rad/s. Tracking rises 0.359 -> 0.491. 16 envs x 3 seeds, 0 ms delay. So the drift was never a capacity problem or a reward-shaping problem; it was a missing control law. Write that down before reaching for another 2000-iteration run.

THE DEFECT AND ITS FIX WERE MEASURED ON DIFFERENT QUANTITIES AND I HAD THEM CONFUSED. `heading_error_deg_median` in `tools/robustness.py` is `atan2(|lateral|, |progress|)` -- a PATH angle, not a yaw angle. The 22.4 deg I have been quoting for three rounds is 'the robot's net displacement curves 22 deg off the commanded direction'. A heading-hold controller aims at exactly that (hold the bearing, the path goes straight), which is why it works; but it means the number was never evidence that the yaw state was wrong.

AND THE 22.4 deg WAS ONE SEED. Re-measured at 16 envs x 3 seeds the same policy and condition read 27.8 deg. Every single-seed figure in earlier rounds was optimistic by ~25%; `--seeds` exists precisely because of this and I was reading the one-seed column anyway. Quote the 3-seed number from now on, and treat any 1-seed delta under ~5 deg as noise.

Zero-shot is the floor, not the ceiling, and there is a real reason to train with it anyway: the untrained policy tolerates the loop only up to about 20 ms. Swept at 16 envs x 2 seeds, path error at 0 / 20 / 40 ms of actuator delay -- k=0.4: 10.1 / 18.9 / 18.6 deg; k=0.7: 6.4 / 17.4 / 22.2; k=1.0: 4.3 / 16.4 / 24.1. At 40 ms the k=1 loop is WORSE than leaving it open (16.4). A pure proportional loop stacked on an already lagging plant is exactly what delay punishes, and the fix is either a lower gain or a policy that anticipates the correction -- only training gives the second. Deployed latency is 6-12 ms per the robustness docstring, so k=1.0 is fine on the bench and k=0.7 is the honest default for a robot.

Implemented as `--heading-envs F` (training) and `--heading-hold` plus `--heading-stiffness` (eval), both defaulting to off so every recorded number stays reproducible. Training side: the target is drawn RELATIVE to the heading at resample, +-45 deg, and not as IsaacLab's absolute U(-pi, pi) -- at k=1 an absolute target saturates the clip on 68% of steps, which would train full-rate spinning instead of the small-error correction that a 20-30 deg drift needs. That deviation is deliberate and is pinned by a negative control that swaps the relative draw for an absolute one and requires the check to go red.

Two design bugs of my own, both caught, both worth remembering because they share a shape. (a) `_update_heading` cannot draw its target inside `resample()`: `reset()` calls `resample()` BEFORE `batch.forward()`, so `rot` is still the previous episode's orientation and the target anchors to a stale heading. Split into flag-then-draw. (b) The eval helper re-anchored the bearing on every step, which re-zeroes the error on every step -- the loop reported as closed while commanding exactly nothing, and the first measurement came back bit-for-bit unchanged, which is the only reason I looked. Both are now negative controls ('eval re-anchors the bearing every step'). The generalisable rule: when a control law looks like it does nothing, check it is not being reset to zero before it can do anything.

selfcheck 71 -> 90 (11 on the training-side controller, 5 on the eval-side, 2 on the target distribution and the anchor bug, plus the negative controls themselves). `robust61_u6` keeps running untouched on the pure upstream recipe -- it is now the BASELINE for a one-flag A/B, not the fix. `u7` = the same command with `--heading-envs 0.5` added, same warm start (`robust61_a`), so the only difference between the two runs is the flag.
